Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-A1F3D3C000-86797
Member: Sawyer Alvarez
Requested Service/CPT: 27702 – Total ankle replacement
Date of Notice: 2026-08-11
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-07 (180 days from date of notice, per the denial letter)

To the Cigna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11, reference number POC-A1F3D3C000-86797. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

Cigna's own published Medical Coverage Policy 0285, "Total Ankle Arthroplasty/Replacement" (Effective Date 3/15/2026, Next Review Date 3/15/2027), sets out the medical-necessity criteria that appear to govern this determination. That policy states:

"Total ankle arthroplasty/replacement with a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved/cleared device is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met: • individual is skeletally mature • presence of ONE of the following in the affected ankle: severe inflammatory arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis); severe osteoarthritis; post-traumatic arthritis • individual has moderate to severe ankle pain that: is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration; interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy) • individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty: active infection; insufficient bone/osteonecrosis; loss of musculature in the affected limb/insufficient ligament support; vascular insufficiency in the affected limb; Charcot's or other peripheral neuropathy; neurological impairment; severe ankle deformity precluding proper alignment; malalignment or severe deformity of involved or adjacent anatomic structures (e.g. hindfoot, forefoot, knee); absence of medial or lateral malleolus, or both; poor skin conditions secondary to surgical scars or trauma."

The policy further states: "Total ankle arthroplasty/replacement for any other indication is considered not medically necessary."

I respectfully submit that the clinical record submitted with my prior authorization request satisfies these criteria, as detailed below.

1. Qualifying joint pathology
Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained 2026-06-02 document tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. These findings are consistent with the "severe osteoarthritis" or "post-traumatic arthritis" categories referenced in the policy. [A formal written diagnosis statement from Dr. Duval expressly identifying the arthritis type (severe osteoarthritis vs. post-traumatic arthritis) with corresponding ICD-10 code was not included in the clinical summary provided to me and should be added to the record if not already submitted.]

2. Duration and functional impact of pain
The clinical summary documents 12 months of progressive ankle pain unrelieved by rest, with the patient ambulating with an antalgic gait and limited to two blocks. This meets the policy's example of function-limiting pain "at short distances (e.g., ... limiting activity to two city blocks...)" and well exceeds the required "three (3) months duration."
[The clinical summary provided to me does not contain a specific statement describing how the pain "interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment." I ask that Dr. Duval's office supplement the file with a statement addressing this element specifically, as it is a discrete requirement under Policy 0285.]

3. Conservative therapy
The patient completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance over 10 weeks (2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27), used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29 that provided only 2 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, over the 12-month symptom course, this conservative treatment record — anti-inflammatory medication and physical therapy, as specifically referenced in the policy's list of qualifying conservative measures — spans well beyond the "at least six months" required by Policy 0285, with objective failure documented in the physical therapy discharge note and the medication/injection records.

4. Absence of contraindications
The record confirms no active infection and no untreated substance use. Exam findings show positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion, with no findings of instability, malalignment, or skin breakdown noted in the materials provided. [The clinical summary provided to me does not contain an explicit assessment addressing vascular status, neurologic/Charcot status, bone stock/osteonecrosis, or presence of the medial and lateral malleoli — each of which is a specific contraindication criterion under Policy 0285. I ask that Dr. Duval's office supplement the file with these specific findings, as their explicit documentation appears necessary to demonstrate full compliance with this criterion.]

5. Skeletal maturity
[The clinical summary provided to me does not state the patient's age or otherwise confirm skeletal maturity. This should be confirmed in the supplemental record, as it is an express criterion of Policy 0285.]

Based on the above, and pending the supplemental documentation identified above, I believe the totality of the clinical record demonstrates that the requested total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) meets the medical-necessity criteria set out in Cigna's own Medical Coverage Policy 0285. I ask that Cigna reverse the denial and authorize the requested procedure.

I have attached the following documentation in support of this appeal:
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-29)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-06-02
- [Supplemental statement from Dr. Duval addressing diagnosis, ADL/employment impact, and contraindication findings, to be provided]

Please note that this appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-07). I request written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and a decision within the timeframe applicable to a pre-service medical necessity appeal.

If any portion of this appeal requires clarification, or if a peer-to-peer review with Dr. Duval would assist in this determination, please contact our office at [phone number] to arrange it.

If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I understand that I may have the right to request an independent external review, and I ask that Cigna provide instructions for that process, including any applicable rights through the Ohio Department of Insurance, along with the internal appeal decision.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Alvarez
